catalog_quote: Lembaama, como muitas outras línguas do grupo banto, tem um sistema tonal de dois tons: um tom baixo [ `] e um tom alto [ ´] . ... Os dois tons desta língua são pontuais, isto é, mantêm a mesma altura, no início ao fim de sua emissão. O tom tem uma função lexical: distingue os lexemas (verbos, nomes, numerais, etc). Na combinação dos tons, quando dois tons se encontram na fronteira entre palavras, o primeiro se apaga.
world_status: accessible description is silent on stress

[...] Os dois tons desta língua são pontuais, isto é, mantêm a mesma altura, no início ao fim de sua emissão. O tom tem uma função lexical: distingue os lexemas (verbos, nomes, numerais, etc). new_statements.translation: Lembaama, like many other languages of the Bantu group, has a tonal system of two tones: a low tone [ ` ] and a high tone [ ´ ]. [...] The two tones of this language are level, i.e. they keep the same pitch from the beginning to the end of their realization. Tone has a lexical function: it distinguishes lexemes (verbs, nouns, numerals, etc.). In tone combination, when two tones meet at a word boundary, the first is deleted.

new_statements.rule_in_words: The only accessible primary descriptions (Okoudowa 2005, 2010, Lembaama of Okondja) analyse the language as a two-tone (H/L) lexical tone language with no contour tones; they say nothing at all about word stress, accent or prominence, so no stress rule can be stated.
new_statements.exceptions: None (no stress statement). Tone: word-boundary tone deletion rule; nouns show more tone patterns than infinitive verbs; polysyllabic verbs prefer L.
new_statements.domain_note: Tone described on citation-form nouns and infinitive verbs (word level) with a phrase-boundary tone rule; the 2010 thesis marks only H tone in running examples. No word-stress domain discussed.
new_statements.identity_note: The only accessible descriptions (Okoudowa 2005, 2010; Blanchon & Alihanga 1992) are of Lembaama/Mbaama (Obamba, Guthrie B62), spoken at Okondja and Franceville, Haut-Ogooué, Gabon (Okoudowa's own village Entogho/Otala near Okondja; Blanchon & Alihanga describe the Lempiini dialect of Eyuga = Glottolog dialect ampi1238 'Ampiini'), not Mbere proper (B61, Congo; Ndouli 2001 'parler de Tsama'). Glottolog 5.x files all these under mber1257 'Mbere-Mbamba' (ISO mdt), with dialects Ampiini, Lesia, Liengi, Nkomo, Ntaana, Obaa, Okumu, Ombamba-Congo, Osele, Oyuomi.

new_statements.quote: Le lembaama est une langue à tons. Sur le plan phonologique, ceux-ci sont analysés comme étant des tonèmes. les tonèmes permettent de distinguer les syntagmes nécessaires identiques sur le plan segmentale. Ils remplissent ainsi une fonction distinctive [...] il ressort que la langue lembaama utilise deux tonèmes pontuels, c'est-à-dire le tonème haut /H/ et le tonème bas /B/. Ces tonèmes ont été identifié dans les trois positions considérées, à savoir : T1, T2 et T3. [p. 353:] Pour les unités prosodiques, le lembaama atteste 2 tonèmes ponctuels haut /H/ et bas /B/. les tons modulés sont analysées en phonologie, comme étant la combinaison de deux tonèmes distincts HB ou BH.
new_statements.translation: Lembaama is a tone language. On the phonological level these are analysed as tonemes. The tonemes serve to distinguish minimal syntagms that are identical on the segmental level. They thus fulfil a distinctive function [...] it emerges that the Lembaama language uses two level tonemes, namely the high toneme /H/ and the low toneme /B/. These tonemes have been identified in the three positions considered, namely T1, T2 and T3. [p. 353:] As for the prosodic units, Lembaama attests 2 level tonemes, high /H/ and low /B/. Contour tones are analysed phonologically as the combination of two distinct tonemes, HB or BH.

new_statements.relation_note: Same type as the existing statement from Okoudowa 2005 (tone language, two level tones H/L, lexical function, no word-stress statement); the catalog record for Lembaama has an empty rule, and this work gives nothing that would fill it with a stress placement. It adds the detail that the two tonemes contrast in all three syllable positions and that contour tones are analysed as HL/LH sequences.
new_statements.rule_in_words: Lembaama of Okondja is described as a tone language with two lexically distinctive level tonemes (H and L), each attested in every syllable position T1-T3; contour tones are HL/LH sequences. The thesis says nothing about word stress, accent or prominence: the strings accent/accentu/proémin/intensit/stress/tonique/emphase do not occur in any stress-related sense in the 468 pages, and the only 'prosodic units' it recognises are the tonemes.
new_statements.exceptions: none (no stress statement at all); tone: dissyllables use 4 of 8 possible tone patterns, trisyllables 8 (§2.3.1.2, printed pp. 82-87)
new_statements.identity_note: The thesis describes the Lembaama spoken at Okondja (Guthrie B.62), south-east Gabon. Its introduction (printed pp. 13-14) equates lembaama with obamba and lembede/lembere and lists mutually intelligible dialects lempini, leduma, lengaami, lengwale (Gabon) and lembaama-le-dzanaga, lembere/lembidi (Kelle, Wesso; Congo), i.e. the same languoid as Glottolog mber1257 (Mbere-Mbamba), of which ISO mbm Ombamba is filed as a dialect.

tone_statements.citation: [Author not established; possibly J. Niama Niama]. n.d. [2022 or earlier]. Evolution des phonèmes du proto-bantu en lembaama (B62). Paper posted on Academia.edu (document 71358932); original venue not established.
tone_statements.quote: Sur le plan pardigmatique, l’analyse tonologique fait apparaître un tonème haut (H) et un tonème bas (B), chaque phonème vocalique porte obligatoirement un tonème simple. Le lembaama possède un système tonal à deux éléments de base ... Tableau 36. Système tonal du lembaama (B. Okoudowa, 2010, p.36 ). Sur le plan paradigmatique, les tons modulés référencés en phonétique sont des séquences des tonèmes. En effet, le ton montant se combine B+H et le ton descendant est identifié comme H+B.
tone_statements.translation: Paradigmatically, the tonological analysis brings out a high toneme (H) and a low toneme (B); every vowel phoneme obligatorily carries a simple toneme. Lembaama has a tonal system with two basic elements ... Table 36. Tonal system of Lembaama (B. Okoudowa 2010, p.36). Paradigmatically, the modulated tones recorded in the phonetics are sequences of tonemes: the rising tone combines L+H and the falling tone is identified as H+L.
tone_statements.locator: p. 80, sec. 1.2.2.2.3 'Le système tonal'; phonetic four-way list at sec. 1.2.2.1.3 'Les unités tonales', Tableau 33, pp. 76-77
tone_statements.summary: Two level tonemes H and L, one per vowel; phonetic rising and falling (Tableau 33: 4 'realisations tonales') analysed as L+H / H+L sequences. Sketch rests on Okoudowa 2010 (Okondja). Sec. 2.2.3 traces *BB/*BH/*HB/*HH reflexes in B60 incl. Lembaama. Nothing on stress, downstep or floating tones.
